narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Always read the outer scale, whichever way the angle opens.
<bookmark mark='flip'/>Turn the paper so the base arm points left, and the outer scale no longer starts at zero.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Mark one hundred ten there, and the angle you draw is only seventy degrees.
removed_beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble says always read the outer scale; the base ray now points left, and the outer scale there starts at 180 on the base ray; a point marked at the 110 label on it gives an arm that makes an angle of 70°; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, put the protractor on your finished angle and read it again.
<bookmark mark='corner'/>An angle below ninety degrees looks smaller than a square corner. A bigger one looks wider.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the recap board shows the check: put the protractor on the finished angle and read it again; smaller than a square corner or wider than it

old_misconception.wrong_answer: always read the outer scale, whichever way the angle opens
old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu says to read the outer scale every time. When the base arm points the other way, the outer scale does not start at zero there, so marking the reading on it draws an angle that adds up with the right one to a straight angle, and the bubble is struck.
